claim: Supercomputers reach approximately 2×10^16 calculations per second.
originalWording: Supercomputers reach approximately 2×10^16 calculations per second.

sources.title: Spiritual Machines: The Merging of Man and Machine — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: Computers and communications in 2009: numerical hardware estimate

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: A supercomputer sustains approximately 20 petaflops on a named numerical benchmark; this is the explicit hardware-throughput proxy.
reference.rationale: The November 2009 TOP500 leader was under 2 petaflops on LINPACK, below the stated 20-petaflop target. Tianhe-2 exceeded 20 petaflops on LINPACK in June 2013. The numerical forecast was late, not unscorable merely because brain equivalence is debated.

evidence.title: TOP500 — November 2009 list
evidence.note: Jaguar Rmax 1.759 petaflops; Rpeak 2.331 petaflops. Rmax is measured LINPACK performance, not brain emulation.. Jaguar Rmax 1.759 petaflops; Rpeak 2.331 petaflops. Rmax is measured LINPACK performance, not brain emulation.
